practice_span: I have been stitching since I was eight. It has been thirty-four years.
craft_description: I say it is a story stitched into layers of old saris. To children I say, it is cloth that women wrote.
craft_distinct: A whole story is told in small even stitches, and the back is as clean as the front.
motif_meaning: The lotus. It means purity and a new beginning. Red and blue thread feel truest.
motif_story: I stitched a lotus in the centre of a wedding kantha. The bride said, it is like my mother's hand.
colour_change: Earlier the colours came from old sari borders. Now from fast market colours. The stitch is the same.
specialisation: Small even stitches. Our group put the stitcher's name on every kantha.
known_for: Women come to me to draw the designs for large story kanthas.
craft_keep_change: I would keep hand stitching. I would change rushed cheap orders.
local_belonging_phrase: “Kantha is a thing of our homes. We don't throw away old saris, we wrap ourselves in them and stitch stories.”
place_belonging_feeling: In Birbhum courtyards women sat together and did this work. That is the pride.
ecological_input: We dry the kantha in the winter sun. In the rains old cloth gets damp and stitching goes slowly. Thread colours once came from plants.
place_use_moment: I dried a kantha in the winter sun in the courtyard, and sat back to stitch in the afternoon.
place_missing: Without sun the cloth stays damp and the stitching goes slowly.
place_change: Tourists and shops have grown in Bolpur. Houses are rising on paddy land. Girls now sit less in the courtyard and are more on their mobiles.
place_before_after: Earlier everyone stitched together in the courtyard; now each works alone on shop orders.
emotion_about_place_change: “More customers is good. But the chatter of stitching together in the courtyard is gone.”
teacher_name_relation: My grandmother, Sarala Das. Later I learned the large kantha designs from my mother-in-law.
teaching_memory: My grandmother would turn my stitching over and look. Not the front, the back. She would say, “If the back lies, so will the front.” Then she would undo it all.
remembered_phrase_gesture: “Small stitch, big patience.” As she said it, she would tap my finger lightly with the needle's tip.
family_generations: My grandmother, my mother, me. My daughter Riya studies nursing in Kolkata and stitches in the holidays. My daughter-in-law is learning now.
family_line: Grandmother Sarala → mother → me → daughter Riya and my daughter-in-law.
transmission_strength:
Girls of the house learn running stitch and small designs easily, and so do newcomers to our group.

The large story-telling nakshi kantha. One takes a year, and now nobody wants to make a whole one.
teaching_practice: First I teach the straight running stitch, then small flowers.
teaching_scene: I sat on a mat beside my daughter-in-law. My needle and hers moved together.
teaching_difficulty: Money comes late, and handwork takes a lot of time. After the housework, evening stitching also strains the eyes.
primary_material:
Old cotton saris, coloured thread, needle. Now also tussar and new cotton for selling.

Old saris from home and the neighbourhood. Thread from Bolpur market, tussar from Sonamukhi and Murshidabad.
first_contact: As a child I slept under a kantha made of my mother's sari. Touching it brings back its smell and softness.
material_special: A washed old sari is so soft that the needle finds its own way. Once three or four layers settle together, the kantha clings to the body.
material_in_hands: Good cloth stays plump under the fingers and doesn't pull. The needle makes a soft sound going in, and the stitches fall even.
material_spoke: If the cloth puckers or the thread pulls, I know the layers haven't settled. The needle also sticks in new starched cloth.
correction_action: I undo the stitching, spread the kantha on the floor again and smooth it by hand. New cloth I wash twice first.
piece_time: Three weeks for a small kantha, a year for a large story kantha. Never rush setting the layers.
material_change: Tussar and new cloth have replaced old saris.
material_change_reason: City buyers want new cloth, and old saris are harder to find.
material_change_gain:
City people like work in tussar and good fast colours, and I get a better price.

The memory of the old sari isn't there any more. In new cloth a kantha is a thing, not a member of the household.
occasion_of_use:
When a child is born, as a wedding gift, to cover oneself in winter. Also as a seat for guests.

A winter noon, sun in the courtyard, the smell of orange peel, and five or six women holding a kantha together and talking.
use_importance: “If she doesn't give a kantha at her daughter's wedding, a mother's heart isn't full.” The elders of the neighbourhood said this.
use_feelings: Stitching a daughter's wedding kantha holds love and fulfilment.
special_vs_everyday: An everyday kantha is simple and takes a few weeks. A wedding kantha holds a whole life's story and takes a year.
special_object_rule: A newborn's kantha is made only from the mother's old sari. It is not sold outside the home.
special_missing: Without a kantha at the wedding, a mother's heart is not full.
not_for_sale_example: My grandmother's kantha, with the story of her wedding stitched into it.
why_protected: Our family's people are in it. It is a memory, not a thing. A price can't measure it.
safer_alternative: Story kanthas our group makes specially for sale. I can show pictures and videos of the stitching.
pride_source: My back stitching is as clean as the front. That is my pride.
pride_moment: At Poush Mela in Santiniketan a senior artist turned my kantha over and looked at the back. Then he nodded and smiled.
recognition_by_others: That artist, and the women of the group, who now send newcomers to me.
loss_if_stopped: Women wrote their own lives on cloth. Without that writing, their words would be gone too.
loss_picture: Empty courtyards, and women's lives written down nowhere.
key_stakeholder_of_loss: Village women, for whom this is their own income and a way of speaking for themselves.
craft_hours: Five or six hours a day, between housework. Before Poush Mela we stitch late into the night.
change_in_lifetime: Earlier kantha was only for the home. Now it is our income, and women keep money in the bank in their own names.
artisan_initiated_change: I formed a group of fifteen. We set prices together, and every kantha carries the name of whoever stitched it.
desired_keep:
Small even stitches, story-telling designs, and sitting together to work.

Rushed large orders at low prices, and the idea that women's work is worth less.
strength_anchor: My back stitching is as clean as the front. And I can tell a whole story in one design, a story my group carries forward together.
concern_anchor: Machine-made ‘kantha stitch’ is flooding the market at low prices, and weakening eyesight makes large work harder.
shareable_content:
The stitching method, the group's story, the stories of kanthas for sale, and my name.

Pictures of my grandmother's kantha, family stories, and the group members' personal and money matters.
desired_change:
Advance payment for large kanthas, so nobody falls behind during a year's work.

All stitching will be by hand, and the name of whoever stitched it will be on the kantha.
learning_story: Once I made a whole kantha on new unwashed cloth. At the first wash it all puckered, and two months of work were gone. Since then I don't pick up a needle until new cloth has been washed twice.
emotional_story: When my mother fell ill I made a kantha from her sari. She passed away wrapped in it. Riya has it now, she took it to her hostel.
clarification_story:
A buyer said, nobody will see the back, so why spend so much time? I asked them to wrap the kantha around themselves. It's the back that touches your body.

Many think kantha means a poor person's patchwork. It is really the written life of women, and very careful work.
